title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for diabetes and foot numbness.

HPI: The patient is an 82-year-old woman presenting today for a routine follow-up of her type 2 diabetes. She reports stable glucose levels and continues to adhere to her current regimen. She also reports persistent tingling and numbness in her feet, which she describes as a form of polyneuropathy. She notes that these sensations are chronic. She remains ambulatory and denies any acute changes in her mobility or sensation.

Medication List: Insulin, Glipizide, and a daily multivitamin.

Exam: The patient is alert and oriented. Physical exam reveals intact skin and sensation in the lower extremities. Neurological exam confirms diminished sensation in the toes.

Assessment: 1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current dual therapy. 2. Peripheral neuropathy: The patient's symptoms are unrelated to diabetes.

Plan: Continue current medications, including insulin and her oral hypoglycemic. We will continue to monitor her glucose levels and schedule a follow-up in three months to assess the progression of her neuropathy.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
